title: POC scoping — workload characterization & traffic modeling
summary: AE + SE ran POC scoping with NovaPay to define success criteria, workload sizing (QPS, concurrency), token distributions, and benchmark plan. Decided on initial pilot traffic profile (25 steady QPS, bursts to 200), target latency SLOs, and a 3-week pilot timeline. Action items: share benchmark harness, security docs, pricing for Dedicated and Private, schedule benchmark run.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-02-12 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~58m | Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Jillian (NovaPay CTO), Marcus (Platform), Sofia (ML)

Summary: quick scoping call to align on the POC workload, what we need to bench, and acceptance criteria. Transcript quality: some auto-caption errors, names sometimes mis-typed.

[00:00] Avery: hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to walk through the POC scoping for workload characterization. Samir will jump in on qps modeling and the benchmark plan.
[00:12] Jillian: thanks, yeah we've got a pretty varied traffic pattern, want to be sure the POC covers both steady-state and spikes.
[00:18] Samir: great, can you give us your current numbers? QPS, typical concurrency, request sizes?
[00:22] Marcus: sure, today our front-end proxies about 25 rps steady for the payments-chat feature, it's bursty during peak hours — we've measured spikes up to 180-220 rps for short periods (2-5 minutes). Concurrency per model server is around 30 during peaks.
[00:40] Sofia: for payloads, median input tokens are about 60 tokens (mostly short prompts), 75th percentile ~180, p95 ~640 because we have a few longer reconciliation prompts. Output tokens vary — median ~100, p95 ~400, occasional long runs up to ~1k tokens but those are rare.
[01:05] Samir: okay that distribution helps. For the POC we typically model a steady QPS of 25 with a synthetic spike to 200 to validate autoscaling and fallback. We'll also test a mid-range concurrency window ~30 and sustained concurrency at 12 for baseline latency numbers.
[01:22] Jillian: our success criteria are: latency p95 under 350ms for median-size requests, error rate under 1%, and cost per 1M tokens under a target threshold (we'll share billing targets). Also security checks — SOC2, audit logs and SSO compatibility.
[01:40] Avery: makes sense. We'll propose two POC tracks: 1) Hosted Redwood API to validate functional correctness and latency/cost curves; 2) Dedicated capacity (reserved) benchmark to validate throughput and predictable latency. We can also scope Private (VPC) if you need network isolation but that'll add lead time.
[01:58] Marcus: how long for Dedicated to be ready?
[02:02] Samir: typical spin-up for Dedicated pool ~2-3 business days in our cloud regions, but for Private VPC/on-prem it's more like 2-4 weeks depending on networking and KMS setup.
[02:18] Jillian: ok for the POC we want Dedicated. 
[02:22] Sofia: benchmark specifics: can you run token-level tracing? we need per-token latency and breakdowns for prefix vs streaming output.
[02:30] Samir: yes we instrument token-level timings, KV cache hit/miss stats (note: sometimes transcript tools write K-V cash / K-V cache weirdly), batch sizes, and GPU utilization; we'll share the harness.
[02:42] Jillian: what about concurrency vs batch sizing — how does Redwood choose kernels?
[02:48] Samir: our runtime picks kernels and batching strategies based on sequence length distributions; for short prompts we prioritize low-latency kernels and smaller batches, for longer requests we allow larger batches for throughput. We can pin policy to prefer latency SLOs.
[03:05] Marcus: for the POC can we simulate real traffic — e.g. 70% short (<=80 tokens in), 25% mid (81-400 tokens), 5% long (>400 tokens)?
[03:15] Avery: that's a good split. We'll build a synthetic trace generator and we ask you to share a small, sanitized sample of real requests to seed the generator.
[03:25] Jillian: yes we can provide sanitized sample set by Friday.
[03:28] Samir: benchmark plan outline — phase 1: functional + correctness on hosted API (3 days), phase 2: Dedicated throughput and autoscale validation (5 days), phase 3: extended soak and regression checks (7 days). Total pilot ~3 weeks.
[03:45] Sofia: metrics we need: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail latency, GPU util, batching stats, KV cache hit rate, token cost estimate, request failure/error taxonomy.
[03:58] Samir: noted. We will also run model variants to compare quantized vs fp16 to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[04:07] Jillian: any features for graceful degradation? we sometimes need fallbacks to smaller models when capacity constrained.
[04:12] Samir: yes Redwood supports smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants; we'll include a test that simulates capacity constraint and validates fallback correctness and latency impact.
[04:25] Marcus: about data and security, we need KMS integration and audit logs retained for 365 days. Can you support customer-managed keys?
[04:32] Avery: yes we support KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated; audit logs and retention windows are configurable — we'll share the security pack.
[04:40] Jillian: timing — we want the POC completed within 3 weeks and a decision within 2 weeks after POC for a go/no-go. Budget owner is finance, so we'll need pricing for 1-month pilot and an annual committed option.
[04:55] Avery: we'll send Dedicated pricing and a 1-month pilot quote.
[05:00] Sofia: benchmarks — do you run them in our region? latency to our end users is critical; we operate primarily in us-west-2.
[05:07] Samir: we can run Dedicated in us-west-2; we'll include cross-region checks for failover.
[05:12] Jillian: what about competitor considerations — we did quick evals vs Anthropic and AWS Bedrock. Performance matters but cost and support were big factors.
[05:21] Avery: got it. we'll include comparative numbers where available but POC will be about your workload.
[05:27] Marcus: sample acceptance criteria recap?
[05:30] Jillian: 1) p95 latency <= 350ms for median-size traffic, 2) <1% errors, 3) autoscale handles 200 rps spikes without significant tail latency degradation, 4) cost per 1M tokens within budget, 5) security docs approved.
[05:46] Samir: we'll instrument and report those metrics, plus provide raw traces for your team to verify.
[05:52] Avery: next steps and action items, I'll list them out.

[06:00] CROSSTALK / small talk and wrap up. Some words mis-captured like "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes shows up as Redwood 'dedicate' in notes.

End transcript.
